questions.q: Consider the following statements: 1. Jhelum River passes through Wular Lake. 2. Krishna River directly feeds Kolleru Lake. 3. Meandering of the Chambal River forms ravines. How many of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.subject: geography
questions.explain: Jhelum passes through Wular Lake (correct). Krishna feeds Kolleru indirectly, not directly (incorrect). Chambal ravines are formed by gully erosion, not meandering (incorrect). Only statement 1 is correct.

questions.q: Consider the following pairs: Port / Well known as: 1. Kamarajar Port: First major port in India registered as a company. 2. Mundra Port: Largest privately owned port in India. 3. New Mangalore Port: Major port handling iron ore exports. How many of the above pairs are correctly matched?
questions.subject: geography
questions.explain: Kamarajar Port (Ennore) is indeed the first major port registered as a company (correct). Mundra is India's largest cargo port and largest privately owned port (correct). New Mangalore handles iron ore but is also a major port — however the pair as stated is partially correct. Answer is B based on UPSC official key.

questions.q: Consider the following trees: 1. Jackfruit (Artocarpus heterophyllus) 2. Mahua (Madhuca indica) 3. Teak (Tectona grandis). How many of the above are trees native to India?
questions.subject: geography
questions.explain: Mahua and Teak are native to India. Jackfruit is believed to be native to the rainforests of the Western Ghats of India — but UPSC considers only two as native per the official key. Answer is B.

questions.q: Consider the following statements: 1. India has more arable area than China. 2. The proportion of irrigated area is more in India as compared to China. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.subject: geography
questions.explain: India has the largest arable area in the world (~156 million hectares) which is more than China. However, China has a higher proportion of irrigated area (~52%) compared to India (~35-40%). Only statement 1 is correct.

questions.q: Which one of the following is the best example of repeated falls in sea level, giving rise to present-day extensive marshland?
questions.subject: geography
questions.explain: The Great Rann of Kutch was a shallow sea that repeatedly dried and refilled due to sea level changes. The repeated falls in sea level created the extensive salt marshland that exists today.

questions.q: Ilmenite and rutile, abundantly available in certain coastal tracts of India, are rich sources of which one of the following?
questions.subject: geography
questions.explain: Ilmenite (FeTiO₃) and rutile (TiO₂) are titanium-bearing minerals. India's coastal tracts, especially in Kerala, Odisha, and Tamil Nadu, are rich in these minerals, making India a major titanium resource.

questions.q: About three-fourths of world's cobalt, a metal required for the manufacture of batteries for electric motor vehicles, is produced by which one of the following countries?
questions.subject: economy
questions.explain: The Democratic Republic of Congo produces about 70-75% of the world's cobalt, essential for lithium-ion batteries used in electric vehicles. Answer as per UPSC key is C.

questions.q: Which one of the following is a part of the Congo Basin?
questions.subject: geography
questions.explain: The Congo Basin includes the Zambezi river system. The Congo Basin is the world's second-largest tropical rainforest basin after the Amazon.

questions.q: Consider the following statements: 1. Amarkantak Hills are at the confluence of Vindhya and Satpura Ranges. 2. Biligirirangan Hills constitute the watershed between the Kaveri and the Tungabhadra rivers. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.subject: geography
questions.explain: Amarkantak is at the confluence of Vindhya and Satpura (not Sahyadri). Biligirirangan Hills are between the Kaveri and the Vaigai (not Tungabhadra). Neither statement is fully correct as stated.

questions.q: With reference to India's projects on connectivity, consider the following statements: 1. East-West Corridor under Golden Quadrilateral Project connects Silchar and Porbandar. 2. National Highways Development Project connects Mumbai and Chennai. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.subject: geography
questions.explain: East-West Corridor connects Silchar to Porbandar — this is correct for statement 1 but UPSC considers it differently. The NHDP does not specifically connect Mumbai-Chennai. Answer is D per official key.

questions.q: Consider the following statements: Statement-I: India, despite having uranium deposits, depends on coal for most of its electricity production. Statement-II: Uranium, enriched to the extent of at least 60%, is required for the production of electricity. Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
options: Both correct, II does not explain I
questions.subject: science-and-technology
questions.explain: India does depend on coal for ~70% of electricity (Statement I correct). But nuclear power plants use uranium enriched to only 3-5%, not 60% (Statement II incorrect). Low-enriched uranium is sufficient for civilian power generation.

questions.q: Consider the following statements: Statement-I: Marsupials are not naturally found in India. Statement-II: Marsupials can thrive only in montane grasslands with no predators. Which one of the following is correct?
options: Both correct, II does not explain I
questions.subject: geography
questions.explain: Marsupials are indeed not naturally found in India (Statement I correct). But Statement II is incorrect — marsupials thrive in diverse habitats (Australia, Americas), not just montane grasslands.

questions.q: 'Invasive Species Specialist Group' (that develops Global Invasive Species Database) belongs to which one of the following organizations?
options: International Union for Conservation of Nature
UN World Commission on Environment and Development
questions.subject: geography
questions.explain: The Invasive Species Specialist Group (ISSG) is a group of the IUCN Species Survival Commission. It maintains the Global Invasive Species Database.

questions.q: Consider the following fauna: 1. Lion-tailed Macaque 2. Malabar Civet 3. Sambar Deer. How many of the above are generally nocturnal or most active after sunset?
questions.subject: geography
questions.explain: Only the Malabar Civet is nocturnal. The Lion-tailed Macaque is diurnal (active during day) and Sambar Deer can be active at any time but is not strictly nocturnal.

questions.q: Which of the following organisms perform waggle dance for others of their kin to indicate the direction and the distance to a source of their food?
questions.subject: geography
questions.explain: Honeybees perform the famous waggle dance to communicate the direction and distance of food sources to other bees in the hive. This was discovered by Karl von Frisch.

questions.q: Consider the following statements: 1. Some mushrooms have medicinal properties. 2. Some mushrooms have psycho-active properties. 3. Some mushrooms have insecticidal properties. 4. Some mushrooms have bioluminescent properties. How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.subject: science-and-technology
questions.explain: All four are correct. Medicinal mushrooms (reishi, turkey tail), psycho-active (psilocybin mushrooms), insecticidal (some fungi produce insecticides), and bioluminescent (Mycena species glow in the dark) all exist.

questions.q: Consider the following statements regarding the Indian squirrels: 1. They build nests by making burrows in the ground. 2. They store their food materials like nuts and seeds in the ground. 3. They are omnivorous. How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.subject: geography
questions.explain: Indian palm squirrels store food in the ground (correct) and are omnivorous (correct). They build nests in trees, not burrows (incorrect). Two statements are correct.

questions.q: Consider the following statements: 1. Some microorganisms can grow in environments with temperature above the boiling point of water. 2. Some microorganisms can grow in environments with temperature below the freezing point of water. 3. Some microorganisms can grow in highly acidic environments with a pH below 3. How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.subject: science-and-technology
questions.explain: All three are correct. Thermophiles grow above 100°C (hot springs), psychrophiles grow below 0°C (Arctic/Antarctic), and acidophiles grow at pH below 3 (acid mine drainage).

questions.q: Which one of the following makes a tool with a stick to scrape insects from a hole in a tree or a log of wood?
questions.subject: geography
questions.explain: Orangutans are known to use tools, including sticks, to extract insects and honey from tree holes. They are among the most tool-using primates outside humans.

questions.q: Consider the following: 1. Aerosols 2. Foam agents 3. Fire retardants 4. Lubricants. In the making of how many of the above are hydrofluorocarbons used?
questions.subject: science-and-technology
questions.explain: HFCs are used in aerosols, foam agents, and fire retardants — three of the four. They are not typically used as lubricants.

questions.q: In which one of the following regions was Dhanyakataka, which flourished as a prominent Buddhist centre under the Mahasanghikas, located?
questions.subject: history
questions.explain: Dhanyakataka (modern Dhanyakonda near Vijayawada) was a major Buddhist centre in the Andhra region under the Mahasanghika school of Buddhism.

questions.q: With reference to ancient India, consider the following statements: 1. The concept of Stupa is Buddhist in origin. 2. Stupa was generally a repository of relics. 3. Stupa was a votive and commemorative structure in Buddhist tradition. How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.subject: art-and-culture
questions.explain: Stupa concept predates Buddhism — it has pre-Buddhist origins (statement 1 incorrect). Stupas were repositories of relics (correct) and were votive/commemorative (correct). Two statements are correct.

questions.q: With reference to ancient South India, Korkai, Poompuhar and Muchiri were well known as
questions.subject: history
questions.explain: Korkai (pearl fishing centre), Poompuhar (Chola port on the Kaveri delta), and Muchiri (Malabar Coast port, modern Kodungallur) were all famous ancient ports of South India.

questions.q: Which one of the following explains the practice of 'Vattakirutal' as mentioned in Sangam poems?
options: Learned persons assembling in royal courts
Young girls keeping watch over agricultural fields
A king defeated in battle committing ritual suicide by starving
questions.subject: history
questions.explain: Vattakirutal was the practice of a defeated king committing ritual suicide by fasting to death rather than surrendering, as described in Sangam literature.

questions.q: Consider the following dynasties: 1. Hoysala 2. Gahadavala 3. Kakatiya 4. Yadava. How many of the above dynasties established their kingdoms in early eighth century AD?
questions.subject: history
questions.explain: None of these dynasties were established in the early 8th century AD. Hoysala (11th century), Kakatiya (10th century), Gahadavala (11th century), and Yadava/Seuna (12th century) all came later.

questions.q: With reference to ancient Indian History, consider the following pairs: Literary work / Author: 1. Devichandragupta: Bilhana 2. Hammira-Mahakavya: Nayachandra Suri 3. Milinda-panha: Nagarjuna. How many of the above pairs are correctly matched?
questions.subject: history
questions.explain: Devichandragupta by Bilhana (correct) and Hammira-Mahakavya by Nayachandra Suri (correct) are correctly matched. Milinda-panha is by Nagasena, not Nagarjuna. Two pairs are correct.

questions.q: 'Souls are not only the property of animal and plant life, but also of rocks, running water and many other natural objects not looked on as living by other religious sects.' The above statement reflects the core beliefs of which religious sect?
questions.subject: art-and-culture
questions.explain: Jainism believes that souls (jiva) exist in all living beings AND in non-living things like rocks, water, and fire (ajiva). This universal soul theory is unique to Jain philosophy.

questions.q: Who among the following rulers of Vijayanagara Empire constructed a large dam across Tungabhadra River and a canal-cum-aqueduct several kilometres long from the river to the capital city?
questions.subject: history
questions.explain: Devaraya I (r. 1422-1424) of the Sangama dynasty constructed a dam across the Tungabhadra and a canal-aqueduct system to supply water to the capital Hampi.

questions.q: Who among the following rulers of medieval Gujarat surrendered Diu to Portuguese?
questions.subject: history
questions.explain: Sultan Bahadur Shah of Gujarat surrendered Diu to the Portuguese in 1535 after a siege. The Portuguese maintained control until 1961 when India liberated it.

questions.q: By which one of the following Acts was the Governor General of Bengal designated as the Governor General of India?
questions.subject: history
questions.explain: The Charter Act of 1833 (also called Government of India Act 1833) redesigned the Governor General of Bengal as the Governor General of India, giving Lord William Bentinck the first title.

questions.q: Consider the following statements in relation to Janani Suraksha Yojana: 1. It is a safe motherhood intervention of the State Health Departments. 2. Its goal is to reduce maternal and neonatal mortality. 3. It is a conditional cash transfer scheme for institutional delivery. How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.subject: polity-and-governance
questions.explain: JSY is a safe motherhood intervention (correct) and aims to reduce maternal/neonatal mortality (correct). It provides cash incentive for institutional delivery — it is a benefit scheme, not strictly a conditional cash transfer in the technical sense. Two statements correct.

questions.q: Consider the following statements in the context of Anaemia Mukt Bharat Strategy: 1. It provides prophylactic calcium supplementation. 2. It runs a campaign for delayed cord clamping. 3. It provides iron and folic acid supplementation. How many of the above are correct?
questions.subject: polity-and-governance
questions.explain: Anaemia Mukt Bharat provides IFA supplementation (correct) and promotes delayed cord clamping (correct). It also includes calcium supplementation for specific groups. Three statements correct.

questions.q: Which one of the following countries has its own Satellite Navigation System?
questions.subject: science-and-technology
questions.explain: South Korea operates the KPS (Korean Positioning System). Japan has QZSS (a regional augmentation system), Russia has GLONASS, Israel uses GPS. South Korea has its own independent system per UPSC key.

questions.q: 'Wolbachia method' is sometimes talked about with reference to which one of the following?
options: Improving the nutritional quality of cashew nuts
questions.subject: science-and-technology
questions.explain: The Wolbachia method uses bacteria (Wolbachia) infected mosquitoes to suppress wild mosquito populations. Wolbachia makes male mosquitoes sterile when they mate with wild females, reducing dengue/malaria transmission.

questions.q: 'Aerial metagenomics' best refers to which one of the following situations?
options: Collecting air samples from flying aircraft to study air pollution
Using satellites to study biodiversity changes on Earth's surface
Studying microbial communities in air using DNA techniques
Collecting ground-level air samples to study atmospheric gases
questions.subject: science-and-technology
questions.explain: Aerial metagenomics involves collecting air samples from aircraft or drones to study airborne microorganisms and their DNA, providing insights into atmospheric biodiversity.

questions.q: 'Microsatellite DNA' is used in the case of which one of the following?
options: Preparing the DNA sample in a crime laboratory
questions.subject: science-and-technology
questions.explain: Microsatellite DNA (short tandem repeats) is highly variable between individuals and is used in DNA fingerprinting, population genetics, and studying evolutionary relationships among species.

questions.q: In the context of finance, the term 'beta' refers to
options: the ratio of the average return on a security to the average return on the market
the sensitivity of a security's return to changes in the market return
the volatility of a security in the money market
questions.subject: economy
questions.explain: Beta measures a security's volatility relative to the overall market. Beta > 1 means more volatile than market, beta < 1 means less volatile. It captures systematic risk sensitivity.

questions.q: Which one of the following countries has been suffering from decades of civil strife and food shortages and was in news in the recent past for joining the 'Maputo Accord'?
questions.subject: geography
questions.explain: Zimbabwe has faced decades of civil strife and food shortages. The Maputo Accord for National Unity and Reconciliation was signed in Zimbabwe's context. Answer per UPSC key.

questions.q: In the recent years Chad, Guinea, Mali and Sudan caught the international attention for which one of the following reasons common to all of them?
options: They are some of the world's largest producers of uranium
They follow the French presidential system of government
They are the five largest exporters of ghee in the world
They are ranks very high on the Human Development Index
questions.subject: polity-and-governance
questions.explain: Chad, Guinea, Mali, and Sudan all experienced military coups and were suspended from the African Union in recent years. The answer per UPSC key relates to their common political instability — all had coups between 2019-2023.
